questions.title: Bitwise AND of Two Unsigned Integers
questions.description:
Read two unsigned 32-bit integers and print their bitwise AND.

Input Format:
Two space-separated unsigned 32-bit integers a and b.

Output Format:
A single integer: a & b.

Constraints:
0 <= a, b <= 4294967295

questions.title: Bitwise OR of Two Unsigned Integers
questions.description:
Read two unsigned 32-bit integers and print their bitwise OR.

Input Format:
Two space-separated unsigned 32-bit integers a and b.

Output Format:
A single integer: a | b.

Constraints:
0 <= a, b <= 4294967295

questions.title: Bitwise XOR of Two Unsigned Integers
questions.description:
Read two unsigned 32-bit integers and print their bitwise XOR.

Input Format:
Two space-separated unsigned 32-bit integers a and b.

Output Format:
A single integer: a ^ b.

Constraints:
0 <= a, b <= 4294967295

questions.title: Bitwise NOT of an Unsigned Integer
questions.description:
Read one unsigned 32-bit integer and print its bitwise complement (one's complement).

Input Format:
A single unsigned 32-bit integer n.

Output Format:
A single integer: ~n.

Constraints:
0 <= n <= 4294967295

questions.title: Left Shift by K Bits
questions.description:
Read an unsigned 32-bit integer n and a non-negative integer k. Print n left-shifted by k bits.

Input Format:
Two space-separated integers n and k.

Output Format:
A single integer: n << k (mod 2^32, as a uint32_t).

Constraints:
0 <= n <= 4294967295, 0 <= k <= 31

questions.title: Right Shift by K Bits
questions.description:
Read an unsigned 32-bit integer n and a non-negative integer k. Print n right-shifted by k bits (logical shift).

Input Format:
Two space-separated integers n and k.

Output Format:
A single integer: n >> k.

Constraints:
0 <= n <= 4294967295, 0 <= k <= 31

questions.title: Sensor Status Bit Check
questions.description:
A microcontroller stores the status of 32 sensors in a single 32-bit register. Read the register value and a sensor index k (0-based). Print 1 if sensor k is active (k-th bit set), otherwise 0.

Input Format:
Two space-separated integers: register value r and sensor index k.

Output Format:
A single integer: 1 if bit k of r is set, else 0.

Constraints:
0 <= r <= 4294967295, 0 <= k <= 31

questions.title: Alarm Flag Set Operation
questions.description:
An alarm subsystem uses bit positions in a 32-bit register to denote which alarms are armed. Read the current register r and an alarm index k. Print the new register value after arming alarm k (setting bit k to 1).

Input Format:
Two space-separated integers: register value r and alarm index k.

Output Format:
A single integer: r with bit k set.

Constraints:
0 <= r <= 4294967295, 0 <= k <= 31

questions.title: Clear Alarm Flag Operation
questions.description:
Read a 32-bit alarm register r and an alarm index k. Print the new register value after disarming alarm k (clearing bit k to 0).

Input Format:
Two space-separated integers: register value r and alarm index k.

Output Format:
A single integer: r with bit k cleared.

Constraints:
0 <= r <= 4294967295, 0 <= k <= 31

questions.title: Hardware Population Count
questions.description:
A digital input module captures 32 input lines packed into a single unsigned integer. Read this integer and print the number of input lines that are currently high (number of set bits).

Input Format:
A single unsigned 32-bit integer.

Output Format:
A single integer: the count of set bits.

Constraints:
0 <= n <= 4294967295

questions.title: Toggle Sensor Bit in Register
questions.description:
A configuration tool toggles (flips) the state of a single sensor bit in a 32-bit register. Read the current register value r and a sensor index k. Print the new register value after flipping bit k (1 becomes 0, 0 becomes 1). Use the XOR-mask idiom.

Input Format:
Two space-separated integers: register value r and sensor index k.

Output Format:
A single integer: r with bit k flipped.

Constraints:
0 <= r <= 4294967295, 0 <= k <= 31

questions.title: Extract Register Bit Field
questions.description:
A network protocol packs a 16-bit header field into a 32-bit word at bit positions [lo..hi] inclusive. Read a 32-bit word w, then lo and hi (0 <= lo <= hi <= 31). Extract the field bits at positions lo..hi and print the field's integer value (right-shifted so bit lo becomes bit 0). Use the AND-mask + right-shift idiom.

Input Format:
Three space-separated integers: w, lo, hi.

Output Format:
A single integer: the extracted field value.

Constraints:
0 <= w <= 4294967295, 0 <= lo <= hi <= 31

questions.title: Parity of Byte Stream
questions.description:
A communication channel transmits bytes and a parity bit is computed as the XOR of all bits in each byte (odd parity = 1 if odd number of bits set). Read n bytes (as unsigned 32-bit values, only low 8 bits used) and print 1 if the total number of set bits across all bytes is odd, 0 if even. Use the XOR reduction idiom.

Input Format:
First line: n. Second line: n space-separated integers.

Output Format:
A single integer: 1 for odd parity, 0 for even.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000, each value in [0, 255]

questions.title: Round Up to Next Power of Two
questions.description:
A memory allocator rounds up a requested block size to the next power of two (1, 2, 4, 8, ...). Read a positive 32-bit unsigned integer n and print the smallest power of two >= n. Use bit-shift operations only. For n already a power of two, output n itself. For n = 0, output 1.

Input Format:
A single unsigned 32-bit integer n.

Output Format:
A single integer: the next power of two >= n.

Constraints:
0 <= n <= 2147483647

questions.title: XOR Cipher Encode and Decode
questions.description:
A simple symmetric cipher XORs each character of a message with a single-byte key. Read a string (no whitespace, max length 100) and a key byte k. Print the encoded (and equivalently decoded) byte values as decimal integers separated by spaces. Use XOR per character.

Input Format:
Line 1: the string s. Line 2: the key k.

Output Format:
Space-separated decimal integers (one per character).

Constraints:
1 <= strlen(s) <= 100, 0 <= k <= 255

questions.title: Reverse Bits in a Byte
questions.description:
A graphics library reverses the bit order of each byte (bit 0 <-> bit 7, bit 1 <-> bit 6, ...). Read a single byte value v (0-255) and print the byte with its bits reversed. Use only bit shifts and masks.

Input Format:
A single integer v.

Output Format:
A single integer: the byte-reversed value.

Constraints:
0 <= v <= 255

questions.title: Russian Peasant Bitwise Multiplication
questions.description:
An embedded firmware cannot use the hardware multiplier for a specific hot loop. Implement unsigned integer multiplication using only bit shifts and additions (Russian peasant method). Read two unsigned 32-bit integers a and b and print a * b. The product fits in 64 bits.

Input Format:
Two space-separated unsigned 32-bit integers.

Output Format:
A single integer: the product a * b.

Constraints:
0 <= a, b <= 4294967295

questions.title: Bitwise Unsigned Division Algorithm
questions.description:
Implement unsigned 32-bit integer division using bit shifts and subtractions (the restoring division algorithm). Read dividend a and divisor b. Print the quotient a / b. Handle b = 0 by printing -1. Do not use the /, %, or * operators; use shifts and comparisons.

Input Format:
Two space-separated unsigned 32-bit integers a and b.

Output Format:
A single integer: the quotient, or -1 if b is 0.

Constraints:
0 <= a, b <= 4294967295

questions.title: Find Lowest Set Bit Position
questions.description:
A scheduler needs to find the lowest-indexed ready task in a 32-bit ready-mask. Read a 32-bit unsigned integer r (non-zero). Print the position (0-based) of the lowest set bit. Implement using the Kernighan trick n & (n-1) to isolate the lowest set bit. Do not use __builtin_ctz.

Input Format:
A single unsigned 32-bit integer r (non-zero).

Output Format:
A single integer: the 0-based index of the lowest set bit.

Constraints:
1 <= r <= 4294967295

questions.title: Hamming Distance Between Codewords
questions.description:
A forward error correction module computes the Hamming distance between two 32-bit codewords (the number of bit positions in which they differ). Read two unsigned 32-bit integers and print their Hamming distance. Use XOR followed by Kernighan popcount.

Input Format:
Two space-separated unsigned 32-bit integers.

Output Format:
A single integer: the Hamming distance.

Constraints:
0 <= a, b <= 4294967295
